clue.text: Reporter beginning to judge yours and my denial

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: first letter of judge
what belongs to you and me together is ours
the simplest word of denial

explanation.surface: A journalist starts judging while flatly refusing something on behalf of the two of us.
explanation.definitionFit: Journo is informal British slang for a journalist, someone who reports news for a paper.

clue.text: Shallow type in drip

indicators.note: one word placed in another ends up enclosed by it

parts.note: to drip slowly through is to seep
a type is a kind

explanation.surface: Some feeble sort of person, a mere drip, is dismissed as lacking depth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drip' reads as an insult for a weak person, but here it is the verb for leaking slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something skin-deep goes no further than the surface, so it is superficial in character or feeling.

clue.text: Beastly campaigner ridiculously maniacal, it impresses one during election

indicators.note: to impress is to press something into a surface, so the one goes inside
something happening during an event sits within it, so these letters sit inside

parts.note: an election is a poll

indicators.note: something done ridiculously is absurdly jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the words taken as written, to be rearranged
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wild-eyed candidate rampages through an election campaign in a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram letters take in an extra I before the whole lot is wrapped in POLL.
explanation.definitionFit: A political animal is a person who thrives on politics; 'beastly' is a playful nod to the animal half of the phrase.

clue.text: Loaded question about dubious tale

indicators.note: one word placed about another goes around it

parts.note: why is a question word

indicators.note: a dubious account is not to be trusted as given, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A leading question is asked about a story that sounds suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaded question' is a set phrase, but 'Loaded' is the definition and 'question' the start of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is informal for having plenty of money, the same sense as rich.

clue.text: Shocking Russian TV with three Liberian plays

indicators.note: plays here is a verb, as letters that play about move freely into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Russian television screens three dramas from Liberia, which some find shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plays' looks like a plural noun for dramas; it is a verb telling the letters to move.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan IV, the sixteenth-century tsar, earned his grim nickname through notorious cruelty, so he is a shocking Russian.

clue.text: Dog in front, great success

parts.note: the bow is the front of a ship
a wow is a sensational hit

explanation.surface: A dog out in front proves a huge hit, perhaps at a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Bow-wow is a nursery or childish word for a canine, imitating its bark.

clue.text: Marine mammal shut up

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flippered sea creature
second meaning: to close something off tightly

explanation.surface: Someone tells a noisy sea creature to be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a flippered sea creature and the act of closing a container firmly.

clue.text: House in Surrey or Kent

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: spans the end of Surrey, all of or and the start of Kent

explanation.surface: An estate agent locates a property somewhere in Surrey or Kent, two English counties near London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' suggests a building; it means a royal dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal dynasty that produced Edward IV and Richard III is the House of that name.

clue.text: Creative work so profound, narrative ends

indicators.note: only the final letters of each word are wanted

parts.note: the last letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A deep piece of writing in which the story finally reaches its conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric poem addressed to a subject is a piece of artistic writing.

clue.text: Shade aggressive, knight knocked out

indicators.note: something knocked out has been removed from where it stood

parts.note: aggressive means violent
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A shady, aggressive character is knocked out by a knight in combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Shade here means colour or hue, and a bluish-purple tint is one such.

clue.text: Country governed by leader in Borneo: that is revolutionary

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Borneo
a country that is governed is run

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so these letters go backwards

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A country on Borneo is ruled by a leader whom some call revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is factually apt: this sultanate sits on Borneo.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a small oil-rich sultanate on the north coast of Borneo, a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Isolated individual, fellow on manoeuvres

indicators.note: troops on manoeuvres move about in new formations, so the letters rearrange

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier off on military exercises becomes cut off from his comrades.
explanation.definitionFit: A lone wolf is an idiom for a person who prefers to act alone, away from company.

clue.text: Picture blown away?

parts.note: surface reading: a painting or photo carried off by a gust
setter's reading: a film whose title describes being swept off by a breeze

explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' is the old word for a film, and the question mark warns that 'blown away' paraphrases a famous title.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1939 Civil War epic starring Vivien Leigh carries a title meaning carried off by a breeze.

clue.text: Fastener in cask pulled up

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulling a word up reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: a tun is a large cask for wine or beer

explanation.surface: A fastening is hauled up from inside a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A threaded metal piece screwed onto a bolt holds parts together, so it fastens.

clue.text: Ramp alongside water, edge cut into rock

indicators.note: something cut into another is set inside it

parts.note: to rock is to sway
a lip is an edge or rim

explanation.surface: A sloping path by the sea where a ledge has been carved into a rock face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like stone; it is the verb for moving to and fro.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipway is a sloping surface leading down to the sea for launching boats and ships.

clue.text: Sign put up in bistro, elevated

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting letters up reads them bottom to top
the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of bistro and the start of elevated

explanation.surface: A notice is fixed high up on the wall of a little restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: The lion is one of the twelve zodiac signs, so this is a star sign.

clue.text: Deceitful behaviour in the last suspect

indicators.note: something suspect is not what it seems, so the letters are not in their true order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The final person under suspicion has been acting sneakily, as in a whodunnit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' reads as a noun for the accused; it is an adjective prompting a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is furtive, secretive conduct, acting so as not to be noticed, hence underhand behaviour.

clue.text: That man's visiting a seedy joint — tacky!

indicators.note: someone visiting a place goes inside it

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar, with a taken as written
that man is he, so that man's is he's

explanation.surface: A man drops into a sleazy bar and finds it all rather vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tacky' reads as cheap and tasteless; it means sticky.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacky in its literal sense means slightly sticky to the touch, like glue that clings.

clue.text: Feeling appendage, all toes bandaged by girl

indicators.note: a wound bandaged by a dressing is wrapped inside it

parts.note: a girl's name
a person normally has ten toes in all

explanation.surface: A girl has all her toes bandaged after an injury, and they hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's antenna is a jointed feeler on the head used for touch and smell.

clue.text: I'm on racehorse, in winds, whatever the weather?

indicators.note: a verb here: what winds about twists and turns into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A jockey declares they will ride their racehorse in any conditions, even in wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winds' reads as gusts of weather; it is the verb meaning twists.
explanation.definitionFit: The set phrase is an idiom meaning regardless of circumstances, much like the definition's own expression.

clue.text: Partner dispatched cheeky ace

parts.note: a partner sent packing becomes a former one
pert means saucy or cheeky

explanation.surface: Someone whose partner has been sent away turns out to be a cheeky tennis player serving aces.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is someone highly skilled at something, a master of their craft.

clue.text: Person stealing money

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who nicks, British slang for steals
second meaning: British slang for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: A thief is caught taking cash.
explanation.walkthrough: To nick is British slang for to steal, and a nicker is slang for one pound.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both someone who nicks things and a slang term for a pound coin.

clue.text: Kind of grey sock dipped in Merlot, say

indicators.note: something dipped in a liquid is surrounded by it

parts.note: Merlot is an example of a wine grape, signalled by say
to sock someone is to hit them

explanation.surface: A sock stained grey after falling into a glass of red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sock' looks like clothing; it is the slang verb for punch.
explanation.definitionFit: Graphite is a dark metallic colour named after the carbon used in pencils, so it is one shade of grey.

clue.text: By the sound of it, travel destination in Italy

indicators.note: we are told to go by how a word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to travel about aimlessly is to roam

explanation.surface: Someone describes an Italian destination on a holiday itinerary.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy's capital is a major tourist city, an obvious place to visit there.

clue.text: Creature a member of religious organisation?

parts.note: someone who is a member of a group is in it
a sect is a religious group

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether some being belongs to a religious body.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the wordplay is a playful reading of the answer as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle, ant or fly is a living thing, so the six-legged animal is a creature.

clue.text: Let me think about that boy, briefly, in Italian region

indicators.note: something said briefly is cut short, losing its end

parts.note: the hesitant noise made while thinking
a boy's name

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates over which Italian region a certain boy comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbria is a landlocked area of central Italy, home to Perugia and Assisi.

clue.text: Nothing new, I left

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone reports there is no news since they went away.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil is a score of zero, a word for none at all.

clue.text: Sight the four of us recalled?

indicators.note: called back means brought back the other way, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: us in the subject form is we
IV is the Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: A group of four friends remembers a scene they once saw.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a scene or prospect seen from somewhere, a sight before the eyes.
